name: list_events
description: List events on the operator's Google Calendar within a time window. Provide time_min and time_max as RFC3339 datetimes; recurring events are expanded into individual instances ordered by start time. Returns a list of event objects (id, summary, start, end, status, location, description, htmlLink, attendees, ...). IMPORTANT — every event carries a free-text 'location' field: that is WHERE the event is, usually a street address the user typed ('1247 Main St W, Hamilton, ON'), sometimes a place or business name or a video-call link. It is the answer to 'where is my meeting / what is the job address', and it is already in the form navigate_device and show_map want — pass it through VERBATIM, do NOT geocode it, look it up, or rewrite it. 'location' is absent or empty on events with no place set (many meetings have none), so check before using it.

time_min.description: Window start (inclusive lower bound) as an RFC3339 datetime, e.g. '2026-06-20T00:00:00Z'.

time_max.description: Window end (exclusive upper bound) as an RFC3339 datetime, e.g. '2026-06-21T00:00:00Z'.

calendar_id.description: Optional. Calendar id to query (default 'primary'). Use list_calendars to discover other calendar ids.

operator.description: Optional. If omitted, resolves to the BlackBox's current operator (single operator auto-selected; otherwise the system default). Do not hard-code an operator name.

returns: JSON array of event objects (or an error string); an empty array means no events in the window. Each event is Google Calendar's own event resource, including: id (pass to update_event / delete_event), summary (title), start and end (each {dateTime} for a timed event or {date} for an all-day one), status ('confirmed' / 'tentative' / 'cancelled'), location (FREE-TEXT address or place — see below), description (notes; job details are often here too), htmlLink, attendees, organizer, creator, created, updated. location is the event's place as the user typed it: a street address, a place/business name, a room, or sometimes a meeting URL. Use it as-is — navigate_device(destination=...) and the show_map intent both take free text and let the maps app do the geocoding, so NEVER convert it to coordinates first. It is simply missing on events with no place set; treat that as 'no address known', not as an error.
example: list_events(time_min="2026-06-20T00:00:00Z", time_max="2026-06-21T00:00:00Z")  ->  first event's 'location' is the job address; navigate_device(destination=that_location, delivery="notify") pushes it to the phone
notes: Requires Google Workspace connected for the operator. Both time_min/time_max must be RFC3339 datetimes (include a 'Z' or timezone offset). Results use singleEvents=True + orderBy='startTime' so recurring series are returned as individual instances in chronological order — index 0 of a whole-day window IS 'today's first event'. Take an event's id and pass it to update_event / delete_event. ADDRESS PATH (the reason 'location' is called out above and in returns): calendar location -> navigate_device.destination is a straight hand-off with no lookup step in between; if location is empty, fall back to reading an address out of 'description', and if there is none, say so rather than inventing one. Four Google protocol keys with no meaning to a reader (kind, etag, iCalUID, sequence) are stripped from every event before it reaches you — they are machine plumbing, and none of the calendar tools accept them; every human-meaningful field Google returns is passed through untouched.
